note: Designer-seeded skeleton, prepared with Finance Operations: the vocabulary of the domain and where each concept lives in the expense system. Deliberately contains NO approval rules - those are what the agent has to learn.

concepts.name: Employee
concepts.definition: A person at Halden & Co. who spends money on the company's behalf and asks to be reimbursed. Expenses carry the employee's first name.

concepts.name: Expense
concepts.definition: One request by an employee to be reimbursed for one expense. It has an amount in EUR, a category, a date, a description, and a flag saying whether a receipt is attached; some categories carry extra details (attendees, cabin and flight hours, nights, vendor, manager approval). It waits in a queue until exactly one decision is recorded for it.

concepts.name: Category
concepts.definition: The kind of expense this is. Halden & Co. uses six: meals, flight, lodging, software, equipment, training. Each category is judged by its own rules.

concepts.name: Receipt
concepts.definition: Proof of payment attached to an expense. The expense shows whether one is attached (receipt_attached).

concepts.name: Decision
concepts.definition: What is recorded on an expense: approve, reject, or escalate to a role. A recorded decision is final.

concepts.name: EscalationRole
concepts.definition: A role an expense can be sent up to when it is not the approver's to decide: manager, director, or it (the IT department).

concepts.name: ApprovalPolicy
concepts.definition: The company's rules that determine which decision is correct for each expense. They are NOT written down in this model: they are learned, from the tutor and from feedback, and then recorded here as rules.
